sources.section: Communication - Email - Mailing Lists and Newsletters
sources.entry: phpList - Newsletter and email marketing with advanced management of subscribers, bounces, and plugins. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: phpList is an open-source, self-hostable email marketing manager for creating, sending, analysing and integrating email campaigns and newsletters.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a web-based and command-line interface for managing subscribers and campaigns. It covers real-time analytics on message responses and subscriber behaviour, and segmentation with per-subscriber content personalisation. A message queue load-balances and throttles multiple accounts and campaigns, tracking each delivery outcome, with domain-based throttling rules. Automated bounce processing uses policy and regex rules and archives every bounce. Campaigns can be scheduled, paused, resumed, repeated and requeued, and subscribers can be imported and exported as CSV or Excel with attributes and preferences. It also includes "Send a Webpage" (remote HTML polling and dispatch), RSS-to-email feeds, attachments, built-in Amazon SES support, and multiple APIs with a plugin-based architecture.
use_cases: manage mailing list subscribers and bounces
send RSS feed updates by email
import and export subscriber lists from CSV or Excel
throttle bulk email delivery through Amazon SES
how_to_run: Copy the files from the release tar file into your webroot (the lists directory).
Keep lists/config/config.php and any edited language files, and copy them into lists/config.
Back up your database before upgrading (e.g. mysqldump).
Open the web installer or upgrade page in your browser and follow the 'Upgrade' link to finish.
Themes can be added by cloning them into lists/admin/ui/ (Trevelin is the default).
stack: MySQL database (implied by the mysqldump backup instructions)
notable: Built-in bounce processing with policy and regex-based handling and archived bounces
Domain-based throttling and message-queue load balancing across accounts and campaigns
Command-line and web interfaces, plus multiple APIs and a plugin-based architecture
Available in 20 languages, with translation handled via translate.phplist.org
Optional hosted version at phpList Hosted alongside self-hosting
caveats: Self-hosting requires setting up a PHP web server and database; the README points to separate requirements and installation sections without detailing them here.
The Dressprow theme is no longer maintained, per the README.
Upgrading from older versions involves manual file copying and a database backup, and may take a long time on large databases.
